raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Let GLM-5.3-Flash's KDA layers use the Kimi-K3 RecoverSSM verify/commit path (`--use-replayssm`) during speculative decoding, so each request holds one KDA state block per group instead of `2 + num_speculative_tokens`. Follows #59147 (which made `--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype` reach the GLM KDA state).

## Claims

- `--use-replayssm` now works for `Glm5NextForCausalLM` / `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` with MTP / DFlash speculative decoding, reusing Kimi-K3's kernels and metadata builder unchanged (no new kernels).
- Per-request KDA state footprint during spec decode drops from `2 + K` state blocks per group to one checkpoint plus small per-draft records (fp32 `[H, K+1, D]` correction and bf16 `[H, K+1, 2D]` key/gate), i.e. about 2.8x less state-pool share per running request at K=4.
- Verify outputs and committed recurrent states match GLM's native per-slot speculative path (`fused_recurrent_kda` with `K+1` state slots).
- `--use-replayssm` without speculative decoding is rejected for GLM (as for Kimi-K3), and RecoverSSM now requires Model Runner V2 with or without prefix caching, since only the V2 runner commits the accepted state after sampling.

## Validation

Unit tests (4x GB300, this branch rebased on main):

```
pytest tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_recoverssm.py      # new: verify + commit vs native spec path, K=4/7, fp32/bf16 state
pytest tests/models/glm5next tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda_metadata.py tests/test_config.py
```

Results on the rebased branch: 523 passed, 22 skipped, 92 failed. All 92 failures are `tests/test_config.py` cases that need Hugging Face Hub access (`Invalid repository ID or local directory specified: ...` under `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1`); the same 92 cases fail identically on `main` in this offline environment (verified by running the file against main's sources, same failure set). `tests/models/glm5next` (incl. the new test), `tests/models/kimi_k3/test_kda.py` and `test_kda_metadata.py` pass in full, as do the RecoverSSM/ReplaySSM cases in `tests/test_config.py`.

`pre-commit run --files <changed files>` passes (ruff, mypy, SPDX, lazy-import checks).

End to end, GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 on 4x GB300 (TP4, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--max-model-len 65536`, MTP `num_speculative_tokens=3`, prefix caching off), native path vs `--use-replayssm`, 64 chat requests at concurrency 16, 512 output tokens each, greedy:

| | native | `--use-replayssm` |
|---|---|---|
| GPU KV cache size (tokens) | 18,198,723 | 23,117,295 (+27%) |
| Max concurrency at 65,536 tokens/request | 277.7x | 352.7x |
| Acceptance length (from `/metrics`) | 2.78 | 2.80 |
| Generation throughput, concurrency 16 | 2,448 tok/s | 2,439 tok/s |

The acceptance length is the direct check that verify sees the right state: a wrong checkpoint or commit would collapse it. Output text was compared as well, but the FP8/MoE serving path is batch-order dependent even on the native build (four greedy copies of the same prompt in one batch diverge from each other after ~13% of the output on both builds), and native-vs-RecoverSSM outputs diverge at the same point (~11%), so the text comparison only shows the two are within run-to-run noise. The step-time trade-off noted below is not visible at this concurrency because the KDA share of the step is small; it is the capacity figure that changes.

Note on the build: the e2e run used the official c077dc663d wheel for compiled kernels with this PR cherry-picked on that commit (no wheel exists yet for the rebased HEAD; the files this PR touches are identical between the two commits apart from unrelated Mamba2/ROCm changes).

## Details

GLM-5.3-Flash's KDA is the same recurrence as Kimi-K3's KDA: l2-normalized q/k, bounded sigmoid gate, sigmoid beta and an `[H, V, K]` state. The only parameter-layout differences are `A_log` stored as `[1, 1, H, 1]` (flattened before the kernels) and a flat `dt_bias`, so the Kimi-K3 RecoverSSM kernels apply as-is.

What changes with `--use-replayssm`:

- **Config**: `validate_mamba_cached_kernel` treats the two GLM architectures as KDA models, so `use_kda_recoverssm` is derived for them exactly as for Kimi-K3 (Triton Mamba backend, PP=1, no stochastic rounding). Both model classes declare `SupportsReplaySSM`. The Model Runner V2 requirement for RecoverSSM, previously only checked with prefix caching, is now unconditional: `commit_recoverssm_state` is driven by the V2 runner's `RecoverSSMState` only, so on V1 decode would continue from a stale checkpoint. KV connectors remain rejected with `--use-replayssm`, unchanged.
- **State layout**: `get_state_shape` / `get_state_dtype` (layer and model-level) append the RecoverSSM correction and key/gate records after the conv and recurrent state, so the Mamba page is `(conv, checkpoint, correction, kg)`; the base shapes are unchanged when the flag is off.
- **Backend**: the KDA layer selects `KimiK3KDAAttentionBackend`, whose builder produces one state slot per request plus the commit plan, and carries GLM's prefill-checkpoint metadata (it is a `GDNAttentionMetadata` subclass). Because that builder leaves `spec_sequence_masks` unset for all-spec batches, the spec/non-spec split is decided by `num_spec_decodes`.
- **Verify**: the spec path calls `kda_recoverssm_verify` (read-only on the checkpoint, writes the per-token records); the accepted state is rebuilt after sampling by the existing `RecoverSSMState.commit_step`. The spec conv window is the verify length `K+1` rather than the state-slot count.

Trade-off: with the Kimi-K3 kernels the KDA part of a decode step costs roughly 1.5x the native per-slot path (verify re-runs the recurrence and commit rebuilds the accepted state). This is a win when decode is bound by state capacity (long outputs, many concurrent requests, larger K), not when it is bound by step time. GLM-specific kernels that close most of that gap are a follow-up.

Not duplicating other work: no open PR touches GLM-5.3-Flash + RecoverSSM (`gh pr list --search "RecoverSSM GLM"`, `"replayssm GLM-5.3"`); the Kimi-K3 RecoverSSM path itself is unchanged apart from flattening `A_log` in the commit context and the unconditional Model Runner V2 check.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to write this change; the submitter reviewed every line and ran the tests above.

When `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` is used with speculative decoding and prefix caching is off, these entries set `use_kda_recoverssm=True` and validation permits the configuration because the runner check below is align-mode-only. detail.title: [Spec Decode][GLM-5.3-Flash] Support KDA RecoverSSM (--use-replayssm)

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,144 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""RecoverSSM on GLM-5.3-Flash KDA matches GLM's native speculative path.
+
+The native path advances one recurrent state per draft position
+(``fused_recurrent_kda`` with ``num_spec + 1`` state slots) and keeps the slot
+of the accepted length. RecoverSSM verifies the same window off one checkpoint
+and reconstructs the accepted state after sampling. Both must give the same
+verify outputs and the same committed recurrent state, with GLM's parameter
+layout (``A_log`` as ``[1, 1, H, 1]``, flat ``dt_bias``) and bounded gate.
+"""
+
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.models.glm5next.nvidia.ops.third_party.kda import fused_recurrent_kda
+from vllm.models.kimi_k3.nvidia.ops import recoverssm as recoverssm_ops
+from vllm.models.kimi_k3.nvidia.ops.recoverssm import (
+    KDARecoverSSMCommitContext,
+    kda_recoverssm_verify,
+)
+
+DEVICE = "cuda"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.skipif(not torch.cuda.is_available(), reason="needs CUDA")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_spec", [4, 7])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("state_dtype", [torch.float32, torch.bfloat16])
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_glm_kda_recoverssm_matches_native_spec(
+    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, num_spec: int, state_dtype: torch.dtype
+):
+    monkeypatch.setattr(recoverssm_ops, "is_conv_state_dim_first", lambda: True)
+    torch.manual_seed(0)
+    num_heads, dim, lower_bound = 32, 128, -5.0
+    query_len = num_spec + 1
+    accepted = [1, 3, query_len]
+    num_seqs = len(accepted)
+    total = num_seqs * query_len
+
+    def rnd(*shape):
+        return torch.randn(*shape, dtype=torch.bfloat16, device=DEVICE)
+
+    q, k, v, raw_g = (rnd(1, total, num_heads, dim) for _ in range(4))
+    raw_beta = rnd(1, total, num_heads)
+    A_log = (0.2 * torch.randn(num_heads, device=DEVICE)).view(1, 1, num_heads, 1)
+    dt_bias = 0.1 * torch.randn(num_heads * dim, device=DEVICE)
+    cu = torch.arange(0, total + 1, query_len, dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE)
+    init = (0.05 * torch.randn(num_seqs, num_heads, dim, dim, device=DEVICE)).to(
+        state_dtype
+    )
+
+    # Native: slot 0 of each row holds the initial state; token t writes slot t.
+    num_blocks = 1 + num_seqs * query_len
+    native_states = torch.zeros(
+        num_blocks, num_heads, dim, dim, dtype=state_dtype, device=DEVICE
+    )
+    slots = (
+        1 + torch.arange(num_seqs * query_len, device=DEVICE, dtype=torch.int32)
+    ).view(num_seqs, query_len)
+    native_states[slots[:, 0]] = init
+    native_out, _ = fused_recurrent_kda(
+        q=q,
+        k=k,
+        v=v,
+        g=raw_g,
+        beta=raw_beta,
+        initial_state=native_states,
+        use_qk_l2norm_in_kernel=True,
+        cu_seqlens=cu,
+        ssm_state_indices=slots,
+        num_accepted_tokens=torch.ones(num_seqs, dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE),
+        sigmoid_beta=True,
+        a_log=A_log,
+        g_bias=dt_bias,
+        compute_gate=True,
+        lower_bound=lower_bound,
+    )
+    expected_states = torch.stack(
+        [native_states[slots[i, n - 1]] for i, n in enumerate(accepted)]
+    )
+
+    # RecoverSSM: one checkpoint block per request.
+    blocks = torch.arange(1, num_seqs + 1, dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE)
+    checkpoint = torch.zeros(
+        num_seqs + 1, num_heads, dim, dim, dtype=state_dtype, device=DEVICE
+    )
+    checkpoint[blocks] = init
+    correction = torch.empty(
+        num_seqs + 1, num_heads, query_len, dim, dtype=torch.float32, device=DEVICE
+    )
+    kg = torch.empty(
+        num_seqs + 1,
+        num_heads,
+        query_len,
+        2 * dim,
+        dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        device=DEVICE,
+    )
+    out = kda_recoverssm_verify(
+        q=q,
+        k=k,
+        v=v,
+        raw_g=raw_g,
+        raw_beta=raw_beta,
+        A_log=A_log.view(-1),
+        dt_bias=dt_bias,
+        lower_bound=lower_bound,
+        checkpoint_state=checkpoint,
+        correction_cache=correction,
+        kg_cache=kg,
+        query_start_loc=cu,
+        state_indices=blocks,
+        spec_query_len=query_len,
+    )
+    torch.testing.assert_close(checkpoint[blocks], init)  # verify is read-only
+    torch.testing.assert_close(out.float(), native_out.float(), atol=2e-2, rtol=2e-2)
+
+    conv_dim, history_len = 12, 3
+    conv_state = torch.zeros(
+        num_seqs + 1,
+        conv_dim,
+        history_len + query_len - 1,
+        dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        device=DEVICE,
+    )
+    layer = SimpleNamespace(
+        kv_cache=(conv_state, checkpoint, correction, kg),

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject GLM RecoverSSM on Model Runner V1**

When `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` is used with speculative decoding and prefix caching is off, these entries set `use_kda_recoverssm=True` and validation permits the configuration because the runner check below is align-mode-only. The MRV1 path in `vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py` never invokes `KimiK3KDAMetadata.commit_recoverssm_state`; that hook is only called by `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_states/recoverssm.py`. Since verify is read-only, accepted KDA state is never folded into the checkpoint and subsequent decode steps run from stale state, so this mode should require MRV2 unless the commit hook is wired into MRV1.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject non-speculative ReplaySSM for GLM KDA**

When GLM is started with `--use-replayssm` but no speculative configuration, `use_kda_recoverssm` remains false, yet this new marker makes model validation accept the flag. In accepted combinations such as FlashInfer, or Triton under MRV1, `Glm5NextLinearAttention.get_attn_backend` returns the normal GDN backend and `_forward` never enters `kda_recoverssm_verify`, so the requested optimization silently does nothing; Kimi-K3 explicitly rejects the same no-spec configuration, and GLM should do so as well.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
